headline: Sales growth accelerates but tariffs and costs cause a loss
summary_short: Mattel's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 10% y/y to $1,125M on Vehicles and Games/Action Figures strength, but a 270bp gross-margin hit from tariffs, inflation, and higher royalties plus a jump in Advertising/SG&A drove Mattel to an $18M net loss ($0.06 diluted loss per share) versus $53M net income a year ago.
summary_long: Net Sales rose 10% y/y (9% constant currency) to $1,125M, led by Vehicles (+14%, Hot Wheels) and Action Figures/Games (+35%, Mattel163 digital games, Masters of the Universe tie-ins); Dolls fell 5% on Barbie softness. Reported Gross Margin fell 270bp to 48.2% on tariffs, inflation, higher royalties, and unfavorable FX, partly offset by Mattel163 and cost savings. Operating Income fell to $11M from $78.5M on higher Advertising and SG&A. Mattel swung to an $18M net loss ($0.06 diluted loss/share) from $53M net income a year ago. Cash fell to $524M from $871M after $100M of Q2 buybacks and Mattel163 acquisition spend. Mattel reiterated full-year 2026 guidance and its $400M buyback target.

drivers.explanation: Net Sales growth accelerated on Vehicles and Games/Action Figures strength, but tariffs, inflation, higher royalties, unfavorable FX, and higher Advertising/SG&A more than offset the top-line gain, flipping the quarter to a net loss.

Driven by a 12% increase in North America and 9% in International; by category, Vehicles (Hot Wheels) rose 14% and Action Figures/Building Sets/Games (Mattel163 digital games, Masters of the Universe tie-ins) rose 35%, while Dolls fell 5% on Barbie softness.
Reported Gross Margin fell 270bp to 48.2% on tariff costs, inflation, higher royalties, and unfavorable FX, partially offset by the Mattel163 contribution and tariff-mitigation/cost-savings actions.
Decrease driven primarily by higher Advertising and SG&A expenses as well as lower gross margin, partly offset by higher Net Sales.
Decline in Reported Earnings Per Share and Net Income was primarily due to the same factors that impacted Operating Income (lower margin, higher Advertising/SG&A).

Cash fell mainly on higher Financing outflows (increased share repurchases, $100M in the quarter) and Investing outflows tied to the Mattel163 acquisition net of cash acquired and higher capital expenditures.
The $598.9M current portion outstanding a year ago has been repaid/refinanced; no current portion of long-term debt remained as of June 30, 2026.
